structuralViolations.clause: §0C.13 (EC-3): "A `COMMIT` whose `confirmation_of_ref.kind !== 'draft'` is mintable **only** when `produced_by_intent_token_hash` is non-null and names a **consumed record whose effect is `REFINE`, `DRAFT`, or — where and only where `confirmation_of_ref.kind === 'approval'` — `REQUEST_APPROVAL`**, and whose capability is the canonical owner's own propose key." §0B.13(3) makes the comparison mechanical: "a `COMMIT` minted for an AE key whose pairing row's `propose` side is not the capability of the consumed … record … is refused."
structuralViolations.conflictsWith: §0.32: "Action Engine capability keys … Only `COMMIT` and `REQUEST_APPROVAL` may carry one, **and they may carry nothing else**." §0B.7 restates it: "only `REFINE`, `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF` and a class-`c` `NAVIGATE` may carry a `C9` ref; only `COMMIT` and `REQUEST_APPROVAL` may carry an `AE` ref." A pairing row's `propose` side is a `CapabilityRef` with `space: 'C9'` (§0B.13(1): "every row's `propose.key` must resolve in `C9_CAPABILITIES`"). Equal precedence: §0C.13 amends the effect set only; it does not amend §0.32/§0B.7's per-effect space rule.
structuralViolations.consequence: EC-3 widened the producing-record set by one effect class but left the second conjunct intact, and that conjunct is unsatisfiable for the class it admitted: a `REQUEST_APPROVAL` record's `capability` is an `AE` ref by construction, while the propose side it must equal is a `C9` ref, and the two spaces are disjoint (§0B.8, verified: AE-CAP ∩ (C9-CAP ∪ TOOL-DEF) = ∅). For the one worked instance, `communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2` is paired to propose key `b35.confirm` (C9) by §0B.11, while the REQUEST_APPROVAL that creates its approval object must carry the AE key itself. The comparison therefore refuses unconditionally, exactly as §0C.12 says §0B.13(3) did before the repair. Consequence: `approve_intent` and `reject_intent` remain unmintable on every `APPROVAL` body, while §0.47 permits the composer to null them only for `state !== 'PENDING'`, TTL passed, or `canDecide` false — the identical structural conflict EC-3 was written to close. EC-3b makes it strictly worse by voiding §0B.13(2)'s `propose: null` escape on the stated ground that "the approval-decision case now has a producing record and therefore a capability to compare" — it has a capability, in the wrong space. §0C.15's sentence "EC-3 makes the decision intents mintable, so the path is no longer circular" is false on the same ground and is itself an unproven normative claim (not separately counted; same root cause). Fail-closed: nothing is admitted; `APPROVAL` simply cannot be emitted with a decision control.
structuralViolations.fix: Amend §0C.13's second conjunct for the `kind: 'approval'` branch only: the consumed `REQUEST_APPROVAL` record's capability must equal the pairing row's **`ae`** side (not its `propose` side), and its `confirmation_of_ref.ref` must name the approval object that record created. Alternatively restore §0B.13(2)'s `propose: null` + `confirmation_kind: 'APPROVAL'` allowance and exempt that row from §0B.13(3). Either edit is one clause; both preserve all four of §0.34's conditions (§0C.14) because a gateway-consumed `REQUEST_APPROVAL` record is still the only admissible producer.

structuralViolations.clause: §0C.17 (EC-4): "const SAFE_PIN_ROLES = ['escape','no_action','reconnect','editor_handoff','discard','remedy'] as const;" with "CLOSED — membership is by role, not by an author's choice, and is checked at build" and "function SAFE_PIN(i) { return SAFE_PIN_ROLES.includes(i.role) && … }".

structuralViolations.consequence: `SAFE_PIN_ROLES.includes(i.role)` cannot be constructed for four of six members, so the build veto EC-4 names as its mechanism cannot be written and `SAFE_PIN(i)` can be true only for `role: 'escape'`. (`'remedy'` is reachable in principle but dead in fact: §4.1.3 L11 fixes the remedy at `effect: 'REFINE'`, §3.2's effect table makes `capability` non-null for `REFINE`, and §0B.7 confines a `REFINE` to a `C9` ref — so it fails SAFE_PIN's third conjunct. L11 is itself unreachable because §0B.37 compiles `on_expiry` as a per-kind constant and assigns `collapse_to_summary` to no kind.) EC-4 therefore closes the escape-verb half of its own defect list and none of the rest: §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 (`reconnect_intent` … "below that floor it is the only interactive element retained", while `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED`), §2.6.16 SETTINGS.4 and §2.6.17 FORM.4/FORM.6 (`editor_handoff_intent` / `discard_intent` "survive EVERY step of the degradation ladder") remain contradicted by §4.5.4 step 1 as amended, none has a `reachable_via` by construction, and §4.5.5 C4 still converts those emissions into `LIMITATION`/`HANDOFF`-only envelopes — so a `SETTINGS_DRAFT` or `FORM` still cannot be delivered on a channel capped at `CHANNEL_IDENTITY` (§1.7 K7). §0C.32's claim that EC-4's exemption is "vetoed at build from ever containing an actuating intent" is true but vacuous for four of the six. structuralViolations.fix: Do not simply add the four names to §3.1's union. Adding `'reconnect'` and `'editor_handoff'` would let a `HANDOFF` floor at `ANONYMOUS`, bypassing both `subjectFloor(handoff_capability_ref)` and `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED`; that is fail-closed today (R3.5.1 and §0.27 would refuse the envelope at mint rather than emit it) but it would make `CONSENT_STATE`/`IDENTITY_BINDING` unmintable again, since §0.27 exempts only `role === 'escape'`. structuralViolations.clause: §0C.20 (EC-5): "At EP-REGISTRY-LOAD: every §A1 row whose status is not [EXISTS] must resolve in MECHANISM_GAP_LEDGER under its own gap_key, and every NORMATIVE-PENDING clause must appear in exactly one such row's blocking_rules. structuralViolations.conflictsWith: The contract binds many clauses to MORE THAN ONE prerequisite: S0C.7 "NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-23, P-25"; S0C.11 "on P-11, P-24"; S0C.18 "on P-11, P-19"; S0C.26 "on P-01, P-02, P-30"; §0B.21 "on P-08, P-18, P-23"; §0B.24 "on P-10, P-14, P-23". It is fail-closed, but it makes the whole contract inert rather than pending.
structuralViolations.fix: State the assertion as coverage rather than uniqueness: every NORMATIVE-PENDING clause must appear in AT LEAST ONE row's blocking_rules, and the binding is the pair (clause, p_ref); assert that the set of pairs equals the set of (clause, prerequisite) bindings declared in the text.

securityContractViolations.clause: §0C.26 (EC-9), Gate 8-R (normative): "For a submission whose profile_id resolves to a profile whose carrier tier is SPOKEN and whose intent effect is COMMIT, the gateway refuses unless all four hold: readback_ack is present; readback_ack.readback_ref === record.confirmation.readback_ref; readback_ack.body_hash === record.body_hash; and readback_ack.affirmation is an exact member of the server-published closed affirmation vocabulary."
securityContractViolations.forbiddenEdge: SPOKEN CARRIER → COMMIT WITHOUT READBACK. The gate's antecedent is the submission's profile_id — a value §3.8 R3.8.3 declares "advisory and is not an authority input" ("the binding control on what a channel may do is the server-derived verification_level, not the profile the client names"), which §3.7's IntentRecord does not store, and which §4.5.2 C3 only narrows field-wise rather than binding to the delivery channel. A caller holding a legitimately minted spoken COMMIT token submits it with profile_id of any RICH_INTERACTIVE profile: the antecedent is false, no readback_ack is demanded, and the COMMIT proceeds to Gate 13 → Gate 14. Unlike CH2's web-push case, there is no mint-side non-existence backstop here, because §4.5.3's SPOKEN row deliberately permits a COMMIT token to exist in the voice channel ("up to COMMIT, readback mandatory"). The only fence on it is this gate, and it is keyed on a field the same client authors. The asymmetry is in the rule, not in the data: the converse clause ("a submission carrying readback_ack where requires_readback === false is also refused") correctly reads the server-set record field that the primary clause ignores. §4.7 V4 is therefore still asserted rather than enforced — EC-9's own diagnosis of the defect it set out to repair.
securityContractViolations.fix: Key Gate 8-R's antecedent on the record, not the claim: "for a submission whose record.confirmation.requires_readback === true" (server-set at EP-MINT/EP-FIT from Lifecycle.delivery_channel, sealed inside body_hash), refuse unless the four conditions hold; treat profile_id solely as evidence for the §4.5.5 receipt and for detecting a renderer that delivered something it should not have.

unprovenNormativeClaims.clause: §0C.11(2): "No floor is lowered. The new formula adds two terms to §0.13's three and removes none: for the 47 keys that are catalogue names the risk term is the same value obtained from the same data, so c9Floor_new(key) ≥ c9Floor_0.13(key) pointwise, by construction. A build assertion states it: ∀ key ∈ C9-CAP ∩ TOOL-DEF : c9Floor(key) ≥ maxLevel(row.min_verification, RISK_FLOOR[riskTier], CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR[row.consent_class])."

'restricted' with RISK_FLOOR['restricted'] = STEP_UP_VERIFIED; §0C.10 replaces it with const risk = def === undefined ? 'ANONYMOUS' : RISK_FLOOR[def.riskTier] — the weakest level in the ladder. The only keys for which that fallback ever fires are the nine C9-only extras, and the build assertion is quantified over C9-CAP ∩ TOOL-DEF, i.e. exactly the 47 keys where nothing changed (verified in process: the catalogue's riskTiers are read 35 / medium_write 7 / low_write 3 / high_write 2, zero restricted). The assertion offered as proof cannot observe the change it is offered as proof of. §0C.11(3) then states the reduction outright — "c9.no_action → ANONYMOUS; b35.preview, b35.confirm, a22.configuration → SESSION_VERIFIED; the remaining five → SESSION_VERIFIED" — and S0C.32 generalises the false half ("No repair lowers a floor, admits a capability, widens an allowlist, or relaxes a veto"), which is also untrue of EC-4's ANONYMOUS exemption. No errata row and no NORMATIVE-PENDING marking covers either sentence; §0C.12 does not list them.
unprovenNormativeClaims.fix: Quantify the no-lowering assertion over all 56 C9-CAP keys against a recorded prior floor vector, and record the nine deliberate reductions as an owner-visible relaxation with their compensating fences named per key (for b35.confirm: approvalRequirement REQUIRED + approverPolicyKey 'tenant-owner' + allowedActorRoles [TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER] at EP-CANONICAL, all four verified in process; for the read keys: an explicit WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY.min_verification row, since c9Floor's other terms cannot fence them).

Does NOT close. Attacked hardest, as instructed. (a) The security question is answered in the affirmative: SAFE_PIN can NEVER carry an actuating intent, and this is provable from the declared shapes, not from the comment. COMMIT/DRAFT are excluded by effect; REQUEST_APPROVAL is excluded because §3.2's table makes its capability non-null and §0B.7 leaves AE as its only admissible space, which the third conjunct refuses; REFINE is excluded identically over C9; CONTROL is admitted but the registry is closed at three keys and the only SAFE_PIN member that can carry one is the escape's control.widget.dismiss, already CONTROL_FLOOR ANONYMOUS. The build veto is genuinely a veto. (b) It DOES lower a floor — to ANONYMOUS, bypassing KIND_FLOOR, subjectFloor and targetFloor together — so S0C.32's blanket sentence is wrong; the residual is targetFloor('s') on a handoff, tolerable only because R3.5.3 never invokes the destination capability and §0.31's routes re-check the principal proof at EP-FETCH. (c) It introduces a new defect and fails to close three of its four clause groups: four of the six SAFE_PIN_ROLES literals are not members of §3.1's closed role union (structural 4), so reconnect, editor_handoff and no_action are still withheld at ladder step 1 and still trip C4.

Four of the six SAFE_PIN_ROLES members — 'no_action', 'reconnect', 'editor_handoff', 'discard' — are values `i.role` cannot take, so no shape in the contract declares them.
structuralViolations.consequence: SAFE_PIN(i) is false for every intent EC-4 exists to rescue except the escape, so EC-4 does not close its own defect. §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 ("below that floor it is the only interactive element retained") and §2.6.16 SETTINGS.4 / §2.6.17 FORM.4 and FORM.6 ("survive EVERY step of the degradation ladder") stay in unsatisfiable conflict with §4.5.4 step 1 ("withhold every intent whose required verification exceeds the session's server-derived level"). reconnect_intent and editor_handoff_intent are class-'s' HANDOFFs and targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED, so on a channel capped at CHANNEL_IDENTITY (§1.7 K7 caps a polling Telegram bot there) both are withheld with no reachable_via, §4.5.5 C4 fires, and SETTINGS_DRAFT and FORM cannot be delivered to that channel at all — which is exactly the failure §0C.16 says it repairs. securityContractViolations.clause: §0C.26 (EC-9): "**Gate 8-R (normative).** For a submission whose `profile_id` resolves to a profile whose carrier tier is `SPOKEN` and whose intent effect is `COMMIT`, the gateway refuses unless **all four** hold: `readback_ack` is present; `readback_ack.readback_ref === record.confirmation.readback_ref`; `readback_ack.body_hash === record.body_hash`; and `readback_ack.affirmation` is an exact member of the server-published closed affirmation vocabulary ... A submission carrying `readback_ack` where `requires_readback === false` is **also** refused."
securityContractViolations.forbiddenEdge: SPOKEN CHANNEL → COMMIT WITHOUT READBACK. §4.5.3's tier table grants the SPOKEN tier an effect ceiling of "up to COMMIT, readback mandatory" — readback is the condition of the grant, not an add-on. §4.7 V4 is the fence ("every COMMIT reached by voice requires readback ... the user confirms the server's sentence, not their own"), and §3.12's own register names "a COMMIT reachable in one tap from a selector, a push, or a spoken utterance without readback" as prohibited. Gate 8-R makes a channel's authority conditional on a value the caller chooses.
securityContractViolations.construction: Gate 8-R's antecedent is the submission's `profile_id`, which §3.8 types as "profile_id: string; // ADVISORY (R3.8.3)" and R3.8.3 declares outright: "`profile_id` is advisory and is not an authority input ... The binding control on what a channel may do is the server-derived `verification_level`, not the profile the client names." By §4.7 V1 and §3.9 Step 0 the voice path resolves to "the same `intent_token` a thumb would have sent", so the COMMIT token minted for a SPOKEN delivery is a submittable opaque handle over any transport. A caller submits that token with the `profile_id` of a RICH_INTERACTIVE profile: Gate 8-R's antecedent is false, the gate does not run, and because a submission carrying readback_ack where requires_readback is false is also refused, the caller must omit readback_ack to pass — so the bypass is not merely permitted, it is forced by the gate's own second clause. No later gate re-imposes the requirement: Gate 5 reads verification_level (R3.8.3), Gate 7 reads the kind's effect ceiling and — per §3.12.1(b) and CH2 — the submitted profile_id again. The commit completes with no readback and no record that one was skipped. The server already holds the correct, unforgeable antecedent: §0C.26 defines `confirmation.requires_readback` as "Server-set; an author cannot write it ... true iff effect === 'COMMIT' ∧ carrier tier is SPOKEN", it lives on the IntentRecord (§3.7, class AUDIT_RETAINED), and the same gate already dereferences `record.confirmation.readback_ref` — it simply does not use `record.confirmation.requires_readback` to decide whether to fire.
securityContractViolations.fix: Key the antecedent on the record, not on the submission: "For a submission whose `record.confirmation.requires_readback` is true, the gateway refuses unless all four hold", and pair it with "a submission carrying `readback_ack` where `record.confirmation.requires_readback` is false is refused". profile_id then stays advisory exactly as R3.8.3 requires, the fence becomes unforgeable because requires_readback is set at mint from the server's own `Lifecycle.delivery_channel` and sealed, and V4's sentence becomes true as written. In the same edit classify the new persisted `readback_ack` members under §4.4.3 (affirmation is CONVERSATION_CONTENT by the same reasoning that classifies spoken_transcript), or §4.4.3 RT5's totality test fails the build.
